summary: Mechanism diagram: non-reference template (identity and RNA yield unknown) -> putative RNA species X -> preferential adsorption at the P-V internal boundary -> reduced effective interfacial free-energy cost -> conditional cavity persistence. Here P is the surrounding RNA-rich phase and V the RNA-poor cavity phase; X is a proposed interfacial layer, not a measured third bulk phase. For a macroscopic X layer between P and V, S_X = gamma_PV - gamma_PX - gamma_XV; S_X >= 0 is the complete-wetting criterion under this three-interface convention. Each gamma and S_X has units of energy/area. The relation is conditional physical reasoning, not evidence that wetting occurs here. The measured observable prediction is a calibrated, sequence-specific boundary/adjacent-dense X signal ratio greater than 1 among cavity-bearing droplets, associated with persistence after conditioning on local bulk signal. Bulk demixing does not require selective boundary enrichment, though incidental enrichment is possible. Smallest discriminating measurement: establish the transcribed X identity, then quantify its signal per calibrated area at cavity boundaries versus immediately adjacent dense phase in the same droplets while tracking cavity persistence. E01 reports only a population mean area fraction; E02 associates template fractions with a distinct endpoint; E03 lacks cavity-state trajectories; E04 measures bulk tie-line endpoints without mapping them to cavity interiors; E05 DNA read fractions do not determine RNA abundance. The returned S1 abstract supports only the broad relevance of coupled associative and segregative transitions in multivalent proteins/nucleic acids; it says nothing about internal RNA interfaces, selective wetting, or the proposed enrichment test. S2 is a broad crowding review and offers no direct support for this mechanism.
